LOT_TITLE: 1959 Porsche 356 A 1600 Cabriolet

LOT_SUMMARY: Fully restored by Dutch Porsche specialist Maurice Felsborg to original specification , Finished in its as-delivered shade of Ivory over a Black-upholstered interior and Black soft top , First delivered to the United States via Max Hoffman , Includes a digital copy of its Kardex confirming original build details

LOT_DESCRIPTION: Chassis No. 151412, In the spring of 1950, Porsche insiders believed they might sell as many as 500 examples of their new 356, with the head of Porsche Press Department Richard von Frankenberg confidently predicting “certainly not more than 500 cars in the first two years.” Reality quickly eclipsed expectations: by March 1951 the 500th German-built 356 was completed, and by 1956 more than 10,000 had left Stuttgart, cementing Porsche's role in the West German Economic Miracle. , Introduced for the 1956 model year, the 356 A marked a decisive break from the Stuttgart brand's Volkswagen-based origins, with Porsche-engineered components refined through extensive road and racing experience. By 1959, the final year of 356 A production, Porsche offered a mature suite of models consisting of the all-weather Coupe, pared-down Convertible D, and luxurious Convertible—light, precise, and engineered with the same methodical rigor prized by the scientists, engineers, and professionals who first embraced the marque. , According to a digital copy of its Kardex warranty card, this 1959 Porsche 356 A 1600 Cabriolet, chassis number 151412 completed production on 1 December 1958. It left Stuttgart-Zuffenhausen in Ivory, over a Black interior with a Black soft top optioned with U.S.-market bumpers and sealed beam headlights. Furthermore, its Kardex notes that it was first delivered through Max Hoffman's distributor to George D. Pearson of Bakersfield, California.  , After nearly 70 years on the road, this 356 A Cabriolet retains a high degree of correctness due to a full and comprehensive restoration by Dutch Porsche specialist Maurice Felsborg. Felsborg retained the 356's original specified Ivory finish and Black interior (now leather) with Charcoal square-weave carpeting. Both its period-correct 1,600-cc Super engine that dates from a 1958 model, and its four-speed transmission were rebuilt by. The 75-horsepower Super engine provides a welcome 15 horsepower bump over its originally fitted Normal unit. , Numerous books dedicated to the model reveal the hand-built nature of the 1950s Porsche, a product of the nose-to-the-grindstone work ethic that helped return Germany to economic prosperity. Hand-leaded panel gaps, race-engineered components, and tight unibody construction all contribute to the jewel-like quality that makes the 356 difficult to correctly restore. Combining expert restoration, final-year development, and a highly desirable open-top configuration, this 1959 Porsche 356 A 1600 Cabriolet offers its next steward a beautifully made and timeless Porsche experience., PREVIEW DETAILS:

LOT_TITLE: 1954 Bentley R-Type Continental H.J. Mulliner Sports Saloon

LOT_SUMMARY: Optioned from new with the rarely seen four-speed Hydra-Matic automatic transmission , One of 193 Sports Saloons bodied by H.J. Mulliner, Powered by its original matching-numbers 4.9-liter inline-six , Elegant original color combination of Regal Red with a Beige leather interior , Documented with digital copies of its original build records

LOT_DESCRIPTION: Chassis No. BC38D 
, Engine No. BCD37  
, Body No. 5752 , All Continental chassis numbers begin with the “BC” prefix, denoting Bentley Continental, followed by a consecutive sequence that omits “13” and is completed by one of five suffix letters—A through E. Chassis BC38D has the added appeal of coming from the late D and E series cars, which benefit from the added power provided by the enlarged 4.9-liter inline-six compared to the early 4.6. Following the completion of its chassis at Crewe, the Continental was shipped to H.J. Mulliner to be outfitted with Sports Saloon coachwork, the same body design as the R-Type Continental prototype. During its production, the car was specified with scuttle aerial, one fog light for the “offside,” one long range driving lamp for the “nearside,” dash heater, rear blind, slit pockets in the doors, and an organ-type accelerator pedal offset to the right by ¾-inch. Notably, the rarely seen four-speed Hydra-Matic automatic transmission option was selected, which not only aided its ease of operation in London but also gave the car a higher top speed than the manual transmission due to different gear ratios. To ensure only the finest quality work, Bentley representatives supervised body construction, after which each completed car was rigorously tested and inspected before first delivery. , Once the testing was complete, this Bentley was sent to George Newman & Co of London and delivered on 1 January 1955 to Samuel John Harris Esq. of Cinema Press Ltd., where he registered the Continental at both his home address and at "The Cinema" in London's fashionable West End. Following Harris, the car went to Guy Howard Martineau, who previously was the U.K. importer and distributor of the French-built Salmson Motors.  The Bentley then passed through a chain of documented owners until January 1964 when it was acquired by Aubrey D Forshaw, the Managing Director of Pan Books, who were the publishers of the paperback editions of Ian Fleming's James Bond novels. Forshaw wasn't just simply Fleming's publisher. Forshaw was Fleming's expert on Bond's cars and possibly drew inspiration to purchase chassis number BC38D from the description of Bond's “The Locomotive” as described in three of the novels. , Previous research shows that this Bentley entered the Fouladi family collection in 1980, where by 2005 it was under the care of Darius Fouladi. Under their care and years of faithful service, Bentley was taken to the experts at Clark and Carter of Cressing, Braintree, Essex, for a major service in August 2014. This work included overhauling the front suspension, repairing the exhaust, and replacing the water pump. The engine sump and the brake system required repairs, and the front wheel cylinders were replaced, and the brake servo was overhauled. In total, nearly £18,000 was on this major mechanical service. Before the end of the year, the car is noted as passing to his now ex-wife, Fary Mythen Fouladi, with it being acquired by the current owner and consignor in July 2024 after a remarkable 44 years under the care of a single family.  , With low production and exceptional design, the Bentley R-Type Continental is a cornerstone of any significant Bentley collection. Celebrated for effortless high-speed touring, it pairs a smooth 4.9-liter inline six-cylinder engine with a rarely seen automatic transmission with exemplary road manners. Widely regarded by enthusiasts as the model to own and drive, it offers its next custodian rarity, timeless elegance, rewarding driving experience, and its connection to none other than James Bond's “The Locomotive.”, PREVIEW DETAILS:
